title: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
summary: SMTP is the protocol for sending email. Commands: HELO/EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, RSET, NOOP, QUIT, VRFY, EXPN. Responses: 3-digit codes (220 service ready, 250 OK, 354 start mail input, 421 service not available, 450 mailbox unavailable, 550 mailbox not found). ESMTP extensions: STARTTLS (upgrade to TLS), AUTH (authentication), SIZE (message size limit), PIPELINING (batch commands), 8BITMIME, SMTPUTF8.

structure.meaning: Identify the client. EHLO enables ESMTP extensions.
Specify recipient. RCPT TO:<recipient@example.com>. Can be repeated.
Start message body. Server responds 354. Client sends headers + blank line + body, terminated by \.\r\n.
Upgrade connection to TLS. Server responds 220. Client sends TLS ClientHello.
Authentication: AUTH PLAIN, AUTH LOGIN, AUTH XOAUTH2. Client sends credentials.
220 service ready, 250 OK, 354 start mail input, 421 service not available, 450 mailbox unavailable, 550 mailbox not found, 552 exceeded storage, 554 transaction failed.

notes: SMTP is a push protocol: sender pushes email to recipient's server.
IMAP/POP3 are pull protocols: recipient pulls email from server.
DKIM, SPF, DMARC are email authentication mechanisms.
SMTPUTF8 (RFC 6531) supports Unicode in addresses and headers.
